description: Solomon warns against two extremes — not just the obvious one. The performative kind of goodness is its own trap, and it gets talked about a lot less.
excerpt: Trying to be too good, in the sense of trying to earn God's love, is its own kind of trap. It looks holy on the outside. But underneath, it is prideful. It is exhausting. It is performative.
verse: "Pay attention to these instructions, for anyone who fears God will avoid both extremes."
body_html:
You have to read the verses around this one to really get what Solomon is saying.

He is basically warning against two extremes. On one side, being overly good in a performative way. The kind of self-righteous, works-based religion that destroys people trying to earn what only God gives by grace. On the other side, being wicked and foolish. Throwing off all restraint. Living however you want with no regard for God.

Both extremes miss it.

That is what stood out to me. Because we usually only think about one side of that equation. We warn against sin. We warn against not caring. And we should. But Solomon is also warning against the other end of the spectrum, and that one gets talked about a lot less.

Trying to be too good, in the sense of trying to earn God's love, is its own kind of trap. It looks holy on the outside. But underneath, it is prideful. It is exhausting. It is performative. It is trying to prove something to God that He never asked us to prove.

And on the other end, not caring at all is obviously a problem. Living like there is no God. Living like there are no consequences. Living for whatever feels right in the moment.

Solomon says the person who fears the Lord avoids both. The one who truly walks with God is not a Pharisee, and not a rebel. Just a person walking with Him. Real. Honest. Dependent on grace. Serious about obedience. Not trying to earn anything and not trying to get away with anything.

That is the balance. And it is only possible when God is at the center, because the moment you take Him out of the picture, you swing to one extreme or the other. Either you start performing to feel worthy, or you stop caring altogether.
question: Which extreme do you find yourself pulled toward more, and how does the fear of the Lord bring you back to the middle?
